idea.name: BlissProductCompliance
idea.one_liner: AI-native product compliance system of action for consumer-goods wholesalers, importers and marketplaces selling across 2+ jurisdictions (EU27, UK, US).

icp.summary: Consumer Discretionary wholesalers and importers (25 to 1,000 employees) selling food, personal care, pharma, toys, electronics or household appliances into 2+ jurisdictions in the EU, UK or US, with no Chief Compliance Officer. Second segment: eCommerce marketplaces and general retailers (25 to 1,000) with high product onboarding velocity.

hard.reason: Memo SAM definition; below 25 no budget, above 1,000 they have a CCO

hard.criterion: HQ in the US, UK or EU
hard.reason: Regulatory scope of the product (GPSR, UK PRaM Act, US states)

hard.criterion: Sells physical consumer goods (wholesale, import, marketplace or retail)
hard.reason: Product compliance only applies to physical products

soft.reason: Strong signal but hard to filter on; judged by the qualify step
Cannot be filtered in Apollo; use as a tiering signal later

soft.criterion: Recent product launches or catalogue growth

icp.notes: TEST brief drafted from the memo by the build agent, NOT agreed with the user. Do not launch from it.

tier_rules.T1: Budget holder: owner, CEO, COO or operations director at a 25 to 1,000 employee wholesaler or importer. LinkedIn + email + call.
tier_rules.T2: Compliance, quality, regulatory or procurement owner, or any T1-title person at a weaker-fit company. LinkedIn + email.

exclusions.notes: No customer or competitor list supplied for the test.

qualify.icp_one_liner: A consumer-goods wholesaler, importer, distributor, marketplace or general retailer (food, personal care, pharma, toys, electronics, household appliances) that buys and resells physical products across more than one country.
qualifies: Wholesalers, importers, exporters and distributors of consumer products (food, non-perishable food, personal care, pharmaceuticals, toys, electronics, household appliances)
eCommerce marketplaces and general retailers with a broad product range
Brands or sellers that import product from overseas suppliers for resale
disqualifies: Software, SaaS, consulting, agencies, banks or other service businesses
Pure manufacturers that only sell their own single product line with no resale
Industrial, B2B-only raw material or commodity traders (chemicals, metals, fuel, agriculture inputs)
Single-location restaurants, cafes or local shops
qualify.lean_direction: lean inclusive: keep borderline resellers with lower confidence

decisions.decision: US, UK, DE, FR, NL, IE for the test (memo says US, UK, EU27)
Not filtered in Apollo (self-reported labels are unreliable); keywords wide, AI qualify decides fit

_comment: Example brief (the TEST brief used to validate the engine). Copy it, change idea.*, and edit the rest with the user in /iv-brief. Apollo filter keys use Apollo's own names; lib/brief.py lists the allowed ones.

signals.name: engineers
signals.note: Many engineers means they build their own tooling, no ERP problem (Zalando, about 2,000 engineers, is out)

signals.name: sales_share
signals.note: Mostly sales and operations staff fits (Rubix DACH)
